_readme.what: Per-piece weights for every jigsaw template pool in the game (village houses, streets, bastion rooms, T&T buildings...). A village house is not a structure, it is one weighted entry in a pool such as minecraft:village/plains/houses, which is why it isn't in structure_config.json. Mods add many of these pieces in code (IE, Dynamic Village, PneumaticCraft...), so this file is written BY THE GAME at every world load from the live pools; you only edit it.
_readme.edit: "enabled": false removes a piece. "current" is its weight: the chance it's picked each time the pool is drawn is current / (sum of the pool's weights). Leave "original" alone (the mod/vanilla weight, refreshed every load). For a category of pieces (all IE houses, all tech houses) use pool_tags.json, whose multipliers apply on top of current.
_readme.apply: Rejoin the world (or restart the server). patcherMod worldgen/PoolTuner applies this at world load, after every mod has added its pieces, and writes pool_tag_report.md. Only chunks generated afterwards are affected.
_readme.weights: Fractional results (current 0.5, or a 0.5 multiplier on a weight-1 piece) are fine: the whole pool is scaled up (at most x10) so the ratios hold. A pool whose pieces are all removed keeps a single minecraft:empty entry, so nothing crashes; a start pool like that just generates no structure (use structure_config.json to remove whole structures instead).
_readme.keys: Pieces are keyed by template id ("immersiveengineering:village/houses/plains_engineer"). feature:<id> = a placed-feature piece (hay piles, lamp posts), list:[...] = several templates placed together, minecraft:empty = the empty lot, " #2" = a second entry for the same template. "missing": true = you edited it but this load didn't find it (mod removed?); it's kept so the edit isn't lost.
_readme.houses: Village houses live in minecraft:village/<plains|desert|savanna|snowy|taiga>/houses (and .../zombie/houses for abandoned villages). pool_tag_report.md lists, per pool, every piece another mod injected.
